bib.title: GPT-4V(ision) is a Generalist Web Agent, if Grounded

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "GPT-4V(ision) is a Generalist Web Agent, if Grounded" (SeeAct), Boyuan Zheng, Boyu Gou, Jihyung Kil, Huan Sun, Yu Su (Ohio State). arXiv:2401.01614v2, 12 Mar 2024 (ICML 2024 style template; the PDF itself says only arXiv). Year 2024.

COVERAGE: 36 pages. I extracted all 86,452 chars and read the abstract, body (pp.1-9), impact statement, appendices A-I (pp.13-19) and the start of the prompt/example figures. I skimmed the reference list (pp.9-12) and skipped the example-figure text from about char 70,500 (pp.20-36: prompt and screenshot transcripts). I checked that stretch for numeric claims and found none. Extraction was clean.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Oracle grounding on live websites: GPT-4V completes 51.1% of tasks. Setup: 90-task subset, 30 per test split; a human monitors every action and judges success; non-login tasks only; oracle means humans execute the model's intended action.
  number: 51.1%
  quote: "Using oracle grounding further improves the performance substantially, reaching a remarkable whole task success rate of 51.1%."
  where: p.7, section 4.2 (also abstract: "it can successfully complete 51.1% of the tasks on live websites if we manually ground its textual plans")
- Whole-task success, offline vs online (Table 4, p.6). Online is much higher than strict offline for the SeeAct variants.
  numbers (Offline0 / Offline1 / Online): FLAN-T5-XL 4.4 / 24.4 / 8.9; GPT-4 1.1 / 12.2 / 13.3; SeeAct-Choice 3.3 / 12.2 / 37.8; SeeAct-Oracle 13.3 / 27.8 / 51.1
  quote: "SEEACTChoice 3.3 12 .2 37 .8 / SEEACTOracle 13.3 27 .8 51 .1"
  setup: the same 90 tasks, with time-sensitive tasks rewritten (for example flight dates). Offline0 allows no wrong step and Offline1 allows one wrong step. Online is judged by a human.
- Online vs offline discrepancy: the authors say offline underestimates task success because several plans can be valid.
  quote: "the whole task success rate is likely underestimated in the offline evaluation due to the variability in actions and plans."
  where: p.7
- Real (non-oracle) grounding on live sites: SeeAct-Choice reaches 37.8% online, 13.3 points below oracle. It beats GPT-4 (13.3%) and FLAN-T5-XL (8.9%) by "over 20%".
  quote: "SEEACTChoice with GPT-4V outperforms both GPT-4 and FLAN-T5-XL by a large margin of over 20% whole task success rate."
  where: p.7. Note that the intro and conclusion give the gap to oracle as "20-30%" (p.2) and "20-25%" (p.8). Those figures are step-level offline gaps, not the 51.1 vs 37.8 online gap.
- Grounding strategies compared by step success rate (Table 3, p.6). GPT-4V on a 30-task subset per split; columns are Cross-Task / Cross-Website / Cross-Domain.
  numbers: Attribute 16.1 / 12.1 / 19.0; Annotation 20.3 / 13.9 / 23.7; Choice 39.1 / 32.7 / 42.0; Oracle 61.9 / 65.0 / 62.1
  quote: "SEEACTAttribute 16.1 12 .1 19 .0 / SEEACTAnnotation 20.3 13 .9 23 .7 / SEEACTChoice 39.1 32 .7 42 .0 / SEEACTOracle 61.9 65.0 62.1"
  Textual choices is the best and image annotation (set-of-mark style) the worst but one. The paper reports step success rate here, NOT element accuracy, for the strategy comparison. The full-set per-metric table (Table 2) covers Choice only.
- Full-set results with Choice grounding (Table 2, p.6). Columns are Ele.Acc / Op.F1 / Step SR.
  numbers: GPT-4V Cross-Task 46.4 / 73.4 / 40.2; Cross-Website 38.0 / 67.8 / 32.4; Cross-Domain 42.4 / 69.3 / 36.8. Oracle (30-task subset) element accuracy 66.4 / 69.5 / 72.8 and step SR 61.9 / 65.0 / 62.1.
  Other models, Step SR in Cross-Task / Cross-Website / Cross-Domain order: FLAN-T5-XL 53.5 / 41.1 / 38.9; BLIP-2-T5-XL 47.0 / 37.0 / 38.9; GPT-4* 32.3 / 27.0 / 29.7; GPT-3.5* 16.8 / 14.1 / 24.1; Gemini Pro Vision 19.6 / 15.4 / 18.0; CogAgent 17.6 / 13.4 / 15.5; LLaVA-1.5 8.1 / 7.5 / 8.5. (* means a 30-task subset per split.)
  quote: "– GPT-4V 46.4 73 .4 40 .2 38 .0 67 .8 32 .4 42 .4 69 .3 36 .8"
  quote: "– GPT-4V-Oracle* 66.4 79.2 61.9 69.5 78.9 65.0 72.8 73.6 62.1"
  Caution: the Oracle row's element-accuracy cells are scrambled in extraction (66.4, 69.5, 72.8 are the Ele.Acc values for the three splits, interleaved with Op.F1). Check the PDF page before quoting them.
- Oracle step success rates and margins over the second-best method.
  quote: "the model achieves a step success rate of 61.9%, 65.0%, and 62.1% across three test splits"
  quote: "it achieves a 8.4% step success rate improvement over the second-best method in the Cross-Task setting... it leads by 23.9% and 23.2% step success rates" (Cross-Website and Cross-Domain)
  where: p.5
- Choice grounding beats text-only GPT-4 on step SR.
  quote: "it outperforms GPT-4 in step success rate of 6.8%, 5.7%, and 12.3% on three settings"
  where: p.5-6. Choice grounding is "comparable to supervised fine-tuning".
- Failure analysis of image annotation (set-of-mark style). 100 samples with correct action generation but wrong grounding.
  quote: "54% of the errors can be attributed to GPT-4V's tendency of visual illusion... Another 46% of errors are caused by GPT-4V's limitation in recognizing the relative position"
  where: p.7. The model invents a bounding box and label when the target is not marked (the correct output is "NA"), or links a box to the wrong label.
  quote: "the best one organically leverages both HTML text and visuals, substantially outperforming image annotation strategies (Yang et al., 2023a) by up to 10%" (p.2). This is the paper's own summary. Table 3 shows a bigger gap, about 19 points in Cross-Task, 19 in Cross-Website and 18 in Cross-Domain, so the "up to 10%" appears inconsistent with Table 3.
- Why Attribute grounding fails: it relies on heuristic matching of element text and type. Many elements have no text, or the text sits on a nearby element.
  where: p.5. Textual choices still struggle when elements look identical (Appendix G).
- Longer tasks widen the oracle-vs-real gap.
  quote: "the gap between SEEACTOracle and SEEACTChoice enlarges on longer-horizon tasks. This is understandable because grounding errors cascade to later steps"
  setup: Easy 1-4 actions (37 tasks), Medium 5-9 (35), Hard 10-18 (18). Figure 3 is a bar chart whose values are not in the text.
  where: p.7
- Token cost of HTML vs screenshot.
  quote: "423 HTML elements that would require 186,490 textual tokens with the GPT-2 Tokenizer, while requiring only 1,445 visual tokens using GPT-4V's visual tokenizer."
  setup: one example screenshot (Figure 1). Table 1 gives dataset averages of about 4,172 to 4,653 visual tokens against 91k-129k HTML tokens.
  where: p.2
- ICL vs SFT: in-context learning with GPT-4V generalises better to unseen websites and domains, while fine-tuned FLAN-T5 is better on seen websites (Cross-Task). Qualitative, backed by Table 2.
- Qualitative capabilities (case studies, no numbers): world knowledge (IATA code SJD for Los Cabos), predicting website state transitions, error correction after an invalid phone number format, and closing pop-up ads proactively.

LIMITS
- Small online sample: 90 tasks (30 per split), judged by one human monitor. Oracle grounding is also human-executed, so 51.1% is an upper bound, not an autonomous result. The abstract says "if we manually ground".
- Online tests are non-login tasks only. Final submissions, purchases and profile changes are prohibited. Pop-up ads were closed by hand. Tasks invalidated by website change were resampled.
- Table 3 and several Table 2 rows use 30-task subsets, so the numbers are noisy.
- The paper states the overall limit as: "fine-grained visual grounding is still a major challenge."
- Models tested are GPT-4V (gpt-4-vision-preview), Gemini Pro Vision and LLaVA-1.5, all from late 2023. Dated.
- Action generation uses the screenshot only, without HTML.
- Safety concerns are noted in the impact statement. The authors manually validated all actions before execution.
- There is no dedicated Limitations section.
- Latency, cost and reliability are not reported.

BUILDS ON: Mind2Web and MindAct (Deng et al., 2023; the DeBERTa-base ranker, top-50 candidates, multiple-choice grounding); set-of-mark prompting (Yang et al., 2023a); WebAgent (Gur et al., 2023); Pix2Act (Shaw et al., 2023); WebGUM (Furuta et al., 2023); CogAgent (Hong et al., 2023); Ferret (You et al., 2023); BLIP-2 (Li et al., 2023); FLAN-T5 (Chung et al., 2022).

CODE: none. The paper has prompt templates (Tables 6-9, pp.15-18) and gives the action as a triplet (e, o, v). Equation: "at = π(st, T,{a1, a2, ...,at−1})".

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p.1): the SeeAct pipeline. The LMM writes a textual plan, which is grounded to an element and an operation.
- Fig 2 (p.3): the three grounding methods side by side (attributes, textual choices, image annotation) for one action. This is the quickest explanation of the strategies.
- Fig 3 (p.7): online whole-task success by difficulty (Easy/Medium/Hard) for Oracle, Choices, GPT-4 and FLAN-T5-XL. It shows the gap widening with task length.
- Figs 10-13 (Appendix E): examples of invented labels and mislinked boxes.
- Figs 14-15 (Appendix F): planning examples.
- Figs 19-20: path variation and error correction.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. The Table 2 and Table 5 extraction has spacing glitches ("38 .0"), and the oracle element-accuracy cells are interleaved. Figure text in the later pages is run together, with no spaces. The "20-30%" and "20-25%" gap statements are not defined precisely in the text. The "up to 10%" claim disagrees with Table 3. Check the 51.1/37.8 pairing before using it as "oracle vs real" (Table 4, online). The 51.1% is on live sites, while the offline oracle step SR of 61.9-65.0 is a different metric. Table 5 shows the markup ablation: number labels at bottom-left gave Ele.Acc 27.0 and Step SR 24.3, the best markup. Target note path was not opened by me.
